'''Imperial gunners/engineers''' were members of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy's]] [[Starfighter Corps (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Starfighter Corps]] (acting as a special sub-unit of the corps) who manned the various weapons and engine rooms of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire's]] [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]], [[Imperial Military/Legends|military]] bases, and both [[Death Star/Legends|Death Stars]]. The most advanced were involved in the firing and maintenance of the [[Reactor/Legends|reactors]] within the [[Death Star/Legends|first]] and [[Death Star II/Legends|second]] battlestations.

==History==
[[File:Imperial_Navy_Gunner.jpg|thumb|left|300px|A gunner at his post]]
Imperial gunners were recruits from the Imperial Navy's [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] program that were either still in training or washed out. Even though they did not make it into becoming pilots, Imperial gunners nonetheless possessed keen eyes, superior reflexes, and a rapport with specialized equipment, and as such they were tasked to use their skills with weapons to handle the powerful [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]] and [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]] of Imperial [[Starship/Legends|vessels]], such as [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] and [[World Devastator]]s. They were trained in repairing and handling [[Engine/Legends|engine]] equipment, light [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]], light, medium and [[Heavy turbolaser turret/Legends|heavy turbolasers]], as well as ion cannons, missile launchers and tractor beams. As such, their duties included tracking targets during combat, firing at targets, reloading ammunition, and preventing overloads in the weapons systems.<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

On both Death Stars, the gunners, often called Death Star gunners, had the additional job of maintaining a careful balance of energy in the battle station's [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]], avoiding the risk of either an overload of the titanic energies or otherwise it phase imbalances that would result huge internal explosions. Such a job was relegated to those gunners who were of both the highest-rank and the best-trained of their peers. The gunners were trained as a group, and also spent months calibrating weapons and running through countless scenario engagements with battle plans devised by [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Tarkin's]] staff as well as simulated [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] battles against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] in the thousands. As a consequence of the drills, alongside their computer-linked helmets, the gunners could aim, power-up, and fire the superlaser with synchronized precision. 168 Imperial gunners were necessary to man the superlaser's eight [[Superlaser firing station|firing stations]] at the [[Superlaser Fire Control]] for optimum performance, with a minimum of 14 gunners manning each of the controls of the initiator laser cannons. In addition, those Imperial gunners who worked directly in the tributary beam sections often had their backs towards the [[Concave Dish Composite Beam Superlaser|tributary beam]]'s brilliant stream of energy, which made them unable to actually witness the beam directly despite their visors protecting them. In addition, some also had to close their eyes before the beam blazed at full intensity due to some of them not wearing computerized enclosed [[Helmet/Legends|helmets]].

Aside from their role of manning various onboard weaponry for various vessels, they have also been trained with activating non-offensive systems such as [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking devices]]<ref name="Star Wars: TIE Fighter">[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']]</ref> and when deployed on the ground- they would be attached to provide support for other regiments.

==Uniform==
{{Quote|Next time I see you, your ugly mug had better be hidden behind one of those snazzy black visors they wear over there.|Nast Hoberd to Tenn Graneet after the latter's transfer to the Death Star|<ref name="DSn">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref>}}
The Imperial gunners wore black [[Durasteel-toed boots|durasteel-tipped boots]], black bodysuits with a [[Belt/Legends|belt]], and black durasteel gloves.<ref name="ANH" />

[[File:Superlaser_Engineer.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Imperial gunners known as superlaser engineers operated the superlasers on the Death Stars.]]
The most distinguishing part of the gunners was their large [[Color|black]] neutral-alloy [[Targeting computer linkup helmet|helmets]] with a slit-like visor fitted with a [[Polarized lens filter|polarized filter]],<ref name="Handbook" /> designed to protect their eyes from the bright flashes of light from turbolaser and superlaser fire. These helmets were also specialized computer helmets that were equipped with [[Macrobinoculars/Legends|macrobinocular]] [[Macrobinocular viewplate/Legends|viewplates]], [[Sensor array/Legends|sensor arrays]] to assist with tracking fast-moving fighter craft, and sophisticated tracking systems for better fire control assistance, as well as being equipped with a tongue-operated [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]]. These helmets, alongside their extensive drills, also resulted in their working in synchronized precision to aim, power-up, and fire the Death Stars superlasers. The helmets also had a transceiver on the left side, with two lights (the top colored blue, and the bottom colored red) and an [[Antenna/Legends|antenna]]. The front and back of these helmets are adorned with the [[Imperial crest/Legends|Imperial crest]], more specifically the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] variant. Their helmets remained almost exactly the same throughout the [[Fel Empire]], while their uniforms gained more armor than before.

Some uniform variants, particularly among Death Star gunners, also utilized helmets that had their lower faces partially exposed, which was suspected by the Rebel Alliance to be to maintain direct audio communication with fellow gunners during tributary beam firing sessions due to the shaft being filled with static charges. They also possessed protective visors, although they didn't actually have much actual use because they often had their backs towards the superlaser tributary beam when it was being fired.

==Organization==
Imperial gunners used a ranking system similar to that of starfighter pilots, with commissioned ranks such as [[Captain/Legends|Captain]], [[Major/Legends|Major]], and [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]].

==Behind the scenes==
[[Industrial Light & Magic]] modelmakers [[Grant McCune]] and [[Joe Johnston]] played Imperial gunners in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']]. In addition, their helmets were also nicknamed "Beetle helmets" during production of the film.

In land battles in ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', [[Imperial Engineering Corps/Legends|Imperial engineers]] looked identical to Imperial gunners.<ref name="Battlefront2">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> Similarly, the ending to [[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']]{{'s}} Collector's CD-ROM features several Imperial gunners given the order to activate the then-recently stolen ''[[Vorknkx]]''{{'s}} [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking device]] as they were about to make the jump to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], implying that the Imperial gunners did have some engineering roles as well. Their functions on both Death Stars bears similarity to the [[Imperial Navy Trooper/Legends|Imperial Navy troopers]].
